name: The Unconscious Made Conscious: My AKU Story

content.title: The Unconscious Made Conscious: My AKU Story

media.caption: Ephline Akoth Obaso: A courageous leap from classroom teaching to transformational leadership
media.alt: The Unconscious Made Conscious: My AKU Story

content.text: "What have I gotten myself into?" This was the first thought that raced through my mind when I first logged into Aga Khan University's learning portal. The familiar lecture notes were gone, replaced by a new landscape of research, critical analysis and deep reflective inquiry. I knew instantly I was stepping into something far greater than just a master's degree.

I had come here because of the stories - not just stories I'd heard, but the storytellers themselves. The AKU graduates I knew stood out. Their depth of thought and their professional approach to problem-solving showed a profound transformation I was truly yearning for. I was already a passionate educator, devoted to teaching and mentoring, but I craved more. I didn't just want to shape lessons; I wanted to shape entire communities and education systems. AKU promised that evolution, not just educating, but moulding thinkers, problem-solvers, and tech-savvy innovators ready for the modern world of work.

The journey was rigorous. Assignments demanded deep research, long hours of reading, and constant self-reflection. Many nights, I wondered if I could meet AKU's high standards. But slowly, I found my rhythm. The nights filled with journal articles were balanced by lively, perspective-shifting discussions with course participants from across East Africa. These moments of clarity redefined what learning truly meant.

Then came a force of nature: Dr Mweru, affectionately nicknamed "Dr Thorough." Her classes were intense and inspiring. She questioned every claim, every argument, and every idea until our thinking expanded beyond what we thought possible. At first, her rigour terrified me, but over time, I realized she was sculpting my mind - preparing me to argue intelligently and lead with purpose.

This critical foundation prepared me for the course on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), where the seeds of new thinking blossomed. I used to believe that climate change was a topic for scientists, but AKU taught me that education itself is the seedbed of sustainability. The social action project compelled me to step beyond the classroom and into the community. I began seeing myself not just as a teacher, but as a shaper of society.

Today, AKU's influence echoes in everything I do. My teaching is more reflective, my leadership more inclusive, and my outlook is truly global. I now approach every decision with one question: How does this improve lives? AKU has been a personal awakening. It has taught me that growth happens when you are stretched, questioned, and refined. I've emerged stronger, more innovative, and deeply self-aware.

To anyone thinking of joining AKU, I say prepare to be transformed. This programme is for those who want to turn their daily work into a source of profound impact. You don't just earn a degree at Aga Khan University - you rewrite your story.
